Three different evidence questions

a.alt: Three different evidence questions. A mechanism, an association and an individual conclusion are different kinds of evidence. A connection between these questions needs evidence; it is not automatic.

c: Use the question to recognise the scope of a claim. A normal pathway does not prove a defect; an association does not prove an individual cause.
Read the related explanation
Open full-size illustration
Read the image as text
A mechanism, an association and an individual conclusion are different kinds of evidence.
Mechanism
: How can a biological process work? Enzymes, transporters, cells and model experiments.
Association
: What varies together in a study? A statistical result needs its sample, effect and uncertainty.
Individual conclusion
: What does this mean for this person? Clinical and genetic interpretation needs additional evidence.
A connection between these questions needs evidence; it is not automatic.
Make a handover visible

a.alt: Make a handover visible. A practical checklist for following a referral or transfer; ask the service which process applies. A sent message is not the same event as an accepted handover or a completed action.

c: This is a record-organising tool, not a declaration that every referral guarantees treatment. Ask for the actual status and next decision.

A practical checklist for following a referral or transfer; ask the service which process applies.
The sender
: What was sent, when and to whom? Keep the referral, summary and reference.
The receiver
: Was it received and accepted? Separate delivery, triage, acceptance and responsibility.
The next action
: Who does what, by when? Record the plan, contact and how an overdue action is escalated.
A sent message is not the same event as an accepted handover or a completed action.
A short account with useful detail

a.alt: A short account with useful detail. Lead with what has changed and the decision you need; keep the supporting detail available. A clear short account can link to a full chronology without trying to fit everything into one box.

c: A template for structuring an appointment question or written update. It does not replace reporting urgent concerns to the relevant clinical service.

Lead with what has changed and the decision you need; keep the supporting detail available.
Change and impact
: What is different from your baseline? Name the practical effect and relevant dates.
Evidence and uncertainty
: Which record supports which point? Separate observation, your report and a working hypothesis.
Decision needed
: What answer or next action are you asking for? Ask who owns it and when you will receive the answer.
A clear short account can link to a full chronology without trying to fit everything into one box.
